chunks: The Arabs of the desert who had stayed behind will now say to you: 'We were occupied with our flocks and herds and families, so ask forgiveness for us.' They say with their tongues what is not in their hearts. Tell them: 'Who can prevail with God for you if He wishes you harm or benefit? Surely God is well aware of what you do.'
ai.seo_question: What did the hypocritical Arabs say to excuse their absence and what was God's response?
ai.summary: In the context of the Expedition of Tabuk, this verse exposes the 'A'rab (Bedouins) who remained behind, offering excuses of wealth and family that masked their inner hypocrisy. It underscores the divine attribute of 'Ilm (omniscience), affirming that God’s power to grant benefit or cause harm is absolute and not contingent on human excuses, a theme central to Shia exegesis regarding the transition from outward compliance to inward sincerity.
